name: Supplement Safety & Interaction Guardrails
purpose: Keep genotype-informed supplement prompts food-first, lab-aware, medication-aware, and bounded by nutrient safety limits.
principles: A genotype can suggest a question; it cannot establish that a person needs a supplement.
Prefer food and measured deficiency/excess context before supplements when medically appropriate.
Review medications, pregnancy/lactation, kidney/liver disease, allergies, and total intake before starting a supplement.
Do not stack multiple products containing the same nutrient without checking the total amount and upper limits.
Natural or botanical products are not automatically safer than medicines; exact formulation, contamination, interactions, life stage, and infant exposure matter.

rules.label: Selenium / Brazil-nut safety
food_first: Prefer ordinary food sources and measured clinical context over a genotype-driven selenium supplement.
avoid: Do not combine Brazil nuts, multivitamins, thyroid products, and selenium supplements without totaling selenium intake.
Do not use GPX1 genotype alone to justify selenium supplementation.
confirm_with: medication and supplement list
thyroid, kidney, pregnancy/lactation, and clinical context
selenium testing only when clinically indicated

rules.label: Magnesium food and interaction safety
food_first: Favor magnesium-rich foods before a supplement when they fit the user's diet and medical needs.
avoid: Do not exceed the adult upper limit for magnesium from supplements and medicines without clinician guidance.
Do not use supplemental magnesium casually with kidney disease or without reviewing antibiotic, bisphosphonate, diuretic, and acid-suppressing medication context.
confirm_with: kidney function
medication timing and interaction review
symptoms or labs when deficiency is suspected

rules.label: Omega-3 food versus supplement safety
food_first: Prefer appropriate fish or algal food sources when compatible with allergy, pregnancy, mercury, and dietary constraints.
avoid: Do not treat a FADS genotype as proof that a high-dose omega-3 supplement is needed.
Do not start high-dose omega-3 supplements without reviewing anticoagulants, bleeding risk, cardiovascular history, and other medicines.
confirm_with: fish allergy and pregnancy/mercury context
anticoagulants and bleeding-risk medications
dietary intake and lipid/clinical goals

rules.label: Iron supplementation requires evidence
food_first: Use allowed iron-containing foods while confirming whether the problem is deficiency, excess, blood loss, or another cause.
avoid: Do not start iron supplements from fatigue, HFE genotype, or a single SNP without iron studies and clinical context.
Do not take iron alongside interacting medicines without pharmacist guidance.
confirm_with: CBC, ferritin, transferrin saturation, and clinician interpretation
bleeding, gastrointestinal, kidney, pregnancy, and medication context

rules.label: Iron-status marker and supplement safety
food_first: Use allowed iron-containing foods while confirming whether the issue is deficiency, excess, blood loss, inflammation, or another cause.
avoid: Do not use TMPRSS6 or TF genotype alone to diagnose anemia or deficiency or to choose an iron dose.
Do not start or avoid iron supplements from fatigue or a single SNP without iron studies and clinical context.
confirm_with: CBC, ferritin, transferrin saturation, and clinician interpretation
bleeding, gastrointestinal, kidney, pregnancy, diet, and medication context

rules.label: Vitamin D dose and lab safety
food_first: Use measured 25(OH)D and clinical context to guide vitamin D decisions rather than a receptor SNP alone.
avoid: Do not use VDR, GC, DHCR7, or CYP2R1 genotype alone to justify megadose vitamin D.
Do not ignore calcium, kidney, parathyroid, pregnancy, or medication context.
confirm_with: 25(OH)D
calcium and kidney context when clinically indicated
medication and pregnancy/lactation review

rules.label: Vitamin A and retinoid safety
food_first: Use ordinary food sources and read the label carefully, distinguishing preformed vitamin A from provitamin A carotenoids before considering a supplement.
avoid: Do not stack retinol-containing products, cod-liver oil, multivitamins, or oral retinoids without clinician guidance.
If pregnant or potentially pregnant, do not self-start high-dose supplements containing preformed vitamin A; review the exact product with a clinician.
confirm_with: pregnancy, preconception, or lactation context
exact product label and total preformed vitamin A
liver disease and oral-retinoid or weight-loss medication context

rules.label: Iodine and thyroid-context safety
food_first: Review ordinary dietary iodine sources, iodized-salt use, geography, and life stage before considering an iodine product.
avoid: Do not use a thyroid-pathway SNP to justify high-dose iodine, kelp, or sea-moss products.
Do not combine iodine products with antithyroid medicines, ACE inhibitors, or potassium-sparing diuretics without clinician review.
confirm_with: TSH/free T4 and thyroid history when clinically relevant
exact iodine product and total intake from multivitamins or prenatal products
pregnancy/lactation and medication context

rules.label: Zinc dose and interaction safety
food_first: Favor zinc-containing foods and measured clinical context rather than treating a zinc-transport marker as proof that a supplement is needed.
avoid: Do not use chronic high-dose zinc without checking the total intake and the risk of copper depletion.
Do not take zinc with interacting antibiotics or penicillamine without following the product label or pharmacist guidance.
confirm_with: exact dose, duration, and copper-containing products
antibiotic, penicillamine, and diuretic medication context
diet, symptoms, and laboratory evaluation when deficiency is suspected

rules.label: Potassium and electrolyte safety
food_first: Use food and measured electrolyte context first; a high-potassium diet or product is not automatically appropriate for everyone.
avoid: Do not use potassium supplements or potassium-containing salt substitutes with kidney disease, abnormal potassium, or impaired potassium excretion without clinician guidance.
Do not use a blood-pressure or kidney-associated SNP to self-prescribe potassium or a low-potassium diet.
confirm_with: serum potassium and kidney function/eGFR when clinically indicated
ACE-inhibitor, ARB, potassium-sparing diuretic, and other medication context
heart, kidney, liver, diabetes, and dehydration context

rules.label: Calcium, kidney-stone, and medication safety
food_first: Prefer dietary calcium and measured vitamin-D, kidney, and bone context before considering a calcium supplement.
avoid: Do not stack calcium products or use high-dose calcium solely because of a VDR, CASR, or bone-related marker.
Do not ignore kidney-stone history or medication interactions with levothyroxine, dolutegravir, lithium, or quinolone antibiotics.
confirm_with: dietary calcium, serum calcium, vitamin D, and PTH when clinically relevant
kidney function and kidney-stone history
exact medication timing and interaction review

rules.label: Vitamin K and anticoagulant consistency
food_first: Use a consistent, ordinary dietary pattern and disclose vitamin-K supplements rather than treating a VKORC1 result as a dosing instruction.
avoid: Do not start, stop, or sharply change vitamin-K intake or supplements while taking warfarin or a similar anticoagulant without the anticoagulation team.
Do not use VKORC1, CYP2C9, or CYP4F2 raw-array data to set an anticoagulant dose.
confirm_with: exact anticoagulant and current INR/monitoring plan
usual dietary vitamin-K intake and all supplements
prescriber or anticoagulation-clinic guidance

rules.label: Folate and MTHFR guardrail
food_first: Favor folate-rich foods and clinically appropriate fortified foods; do not create a permanent folic-acid avoidance rule from MTHFR.
avoid: Do not avoid folic acid or switch to high-dose methylfolate solely because of an MTHFR SNP.
Do not use high-dose folate without checking B12, medications, pregnancy, and clinician guidance.
confirm_with: folate, B12, CBC/MCV, and homocysteine when clinically relevant
pregnancy or preconception guidance

rules.label: Vitamin B12 status and absorption safety
food_first: Use B12-containing foods or fortified foods that fit the person's diet before treating a common absorption marker as a supplement prescription.
avoid: Do not use FUT2, TCN2, or CUBN genotype alone to diagnose deficiency or choose a B12 dose.
Do not use folate or an energy product to mask neurologic, blood-count, or fatigue symptoms while a possible B12 problem remains unexplained.
Do not stop metformin or acid-suppressing medication because of a raw DNA result; review the indication and B12 status with the prescriber.
confirm_with: dietary pattern, fortified foods, exact supplement label, and total B12 intake
CBC/MCV and serum B12
MMA when serum B12 is borderline or clinical uncertainty remains, with renal context
medication review and clinician evaluation for neurologic or anemia symptoms

rules.label: Vitamin B6 dose and neuropathy safety
food_first: Prefer ordinary food sources and check the full product label before considering a vitamin B6 supplement; a symptom pattern or DNA result does not establish a B6 need.
avoid: Do not stack B6 across a multivitamin, B-complex, energy product, and single-nutrient supplement without totaling the amount and duration.
Do not use high-dose or long-term supplemental B6 to treat cycle symptoms, mood, nausea, or a methylation claim without clinician guidance.
Stop self-directed B6 supplementation and seek medical advice for new numbness, tingling, burning pain, balance changes, or other neurologic symptoms.
confirm_with: exact product labels, B6 form, amount, total daily intake, and duration
new neurologic symptoms and other possible causes of neuropathy
pregnancy/lactation, kidney/liver, and medication context, including cycloserine, theophylline, or seizure medicines

rules.label: Menopause botanicals and hormone-claim safety
food_first: Use ordinary soy foods, adequate protein and fiber, calcium-rich or fortified foods, hydration, and symptom tracking when they fit the person's diet and goals before reaching for a botanical product.
Treat a supplement as a separate product-safety question; the menopause marker pack cannot establish need, dose, efficacy, or hormone response.
avoid: Do not treat black cohosh, isoflavones, red clover, DHEA, wild yam, maca, or an unregulated bioidentical product as proven hormone replacement or a way to balance hormones.
Do not use genotype to start, stop, dose, or substitute a botanical, DHEA, hormone, or prescribed medication.

Use extra caution and clinician or pharmacist review with pregnancy, lactation, hormone-sensitive cancer, liver disease, clotting history, anticoagulants, endocrine medicines, or multiple products; stop and seek care for jaundice, dark urine, severe abdominal pain, or an allergic reaction.
confirm_with: exact product label, botanical species or extract, dose, lot or quality information, and duration
current prescription, OTC, supplement, pregnancy/lactation, cancer, liver, clotting, and thyroid context
clinician or pharmacist review of evidence, interactions, and monitoring

rules.label: Lactation and herbal-product safety
food_first: For feeding or milk-supply concerns, start with a feeding assessment, hydration and regular meals, and lactation or clinical support rather than assuming an herb is needed.
avoid: Do not assume a tea, herb, essential oil, CBD product, or galactagogue is safe because it is natural; infant exposure, contamination, dose, and interactions may be uncertain.
Do not use a DNA result to select a lactation product, alter medication, or promise an increase in milk supply.
confirm_with: exact product label, ingredients, dose, preparation, and timing
infant age, prematurity, health conditions, feeding goals, and the lactating person's medical history
clinician, pharmacist, pediatric clinician, lactation professional, and current LactMed review as appropriate

rules.label: Creatine and kidney-context safety
food_first: Treat creatine as a goal- and training-context option, not a genetic requirement.
avoid: Do not use genotype to prescribe a creatine dose or override kidney disease, abnormal kidney tests, pregnancy, or clinician restrictions.
confirm_with: training goal, hydration, kidney function, and current medications

do_not_do: Do not infer supplement need, safety, dose, or efficacy from a common SNP alone.
Do not treat supplement ideas as medication substitutes or use them to counteract a prescribed treatment.
Do not recommend a supplement while ignoring a user's allergy, eating-disorder risk, kidney/liver disease, pregnancy/lactation, or medication list.
Do not present a botanical or natural remedy as a hormone treatment, detox, or infant-safe product without exact-product and clinical review.
